_schema_notes: Each program: id, name, category[], org_type, agency, benefit, who_its_for, eligibility[], required_documents[], application_process, apply_url, status, confidence, source_url, source_checked, notes. confidence is 'high' (multi-field confirmed on official .gov.ng page) or 'needs_verification' (not yet checked, or official page lacks detail). Never present a 'needs_verification' program in the demo without saying so. access_pathway is one of: self_service_application, registry_gated, automatic_institutional, agency_sponsored, unknown, not_applicable — determines which CTA pattern the card uses (see ClaimAm design findings doc).

programs.name: NELFUND (Nigerian Education Loan Fund)
programs.benefit: Full tuition + up to ₦20,000/month upkeep, interest-free
programs.who_its_for: Tertiary students needing tuition and upkeep support
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Enrolled at a federal or state-owned university, polytechnic, monotechnic, college of education, or vocational/innovation enterprise institution (IEI)
Active, currently enrolled student (not a graduate or prospective applicant)
Valid NIN required
Institution must have uploaded the student's record to the NELFUND Student Verification Portal
required_documents: proof of admission/enrollment (via school's verification upload)
programs.application_process: Register on the NELFUND student portal, verify JAMB/matric number, confirm institution, upload admission letter, then request the loan from your dashboard
programs.status_detail: 2025/26 window ran 23 Oct 2025 – 31 Jan 2026, extended to 27 Feb 2026, then closed. As of Sept 2026 no confirmed 2026/27 opening date found — recheck portal.nelf.gov.ng before demo/launch.
programs.notes: IMPORTANT FIX: the previously recorded apply_url (nelfund.gov.ng) does not resolve (DNS failure) — it is a dead domain, not the real NELFUND site. The correct official domain is nelf.gov.ng, with the application portal at portal.nelf.gov.ng. Anyone who had bookmarked or shared the old .gov.ng-look-alike link should be redirected — this is exactly the kind of stale/wrong link the 'never show a fake Apply now' design principle is meant to catch.

programs.name: N-Power
programs.benefit: Job placement + skills training to increase employability
eligibility: Open to both graduates and non-graduates
required_documents: valid email address or phone number
means of ID (National ID, Voter's Card, Driver's License, or International Passport)
programs.application_process: Register with your NIN (auto-populates personal details), complete the form with contact/education details and BVN, upload documents, then select a primary and alternate programme (e.g. N-Teach, N-Health, N-Tech)
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources only (pbridgeco.com, mediangr.com.ng, recruitnaija.com) — nasims.gov.ng and npower.gov.ng both refused connection on direct fetch, Sept 2026
programs.notes: Documents/process above are corroborated across several independent guide sites, but the actual live portal URL is unresolved — sources conflict between nasims.gov.ng, npower.gov.ng, and npower.fmhds.gov.ng, and none were reachable directly. N-Power also appears to be converging with NSIPA's newer VSTP (Vocational and Skills Training Programme, vstpmedds.nsipa.gov.ng) — worth a live phone check with NSIPA (info@nsipa.gov.ng, +234 802 126 6483) to confirm which portal is current before demo.

programs.name: GEEP — TraderMoni
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Has an existing small trading business
programs.application_process: Visit the NSIPA GEEP info page, then follow the program's current application channel (no stable direct application URL found — see notes)
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (cutoffmark.ng, connectnigeria.com) for eligibility/documents; apply_url corrected 2026-09-17 after a user confirmed geep.nsipa.gov.ng is suspended in production, not just transiently down
programs.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-17: geep.nsipa.gov.ng (used from 2026-09-17 research through the same day) returns 'service has been suspended' in production, confirmed by a real user click-through, not just an automated-fetch fluke. Reverted apply_url to nsipa.gov.ng/geep/, which is live (200) but is an NSIPA info page describing the program rather than a working application form — same limitation the original research already flagged. geep.com.ng (also live) is an alternative info page, same limitation. No genuinely working GEEP application URL has been found yet — needs a live human check before demo, and the card copy should not imply a working 'Apply now' form exists.

programs.name: GEEP — MarketMoni
eligibility: Women engaged in market trading, typically affiliated with a market association/cooperative
Nigerian citizen
programs.application_process: Visit the NSIPA GEEP info page, then follow the program's current application channel (no stable direct application URL found — see notes)
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (cutoffmark.ng, connectnigeria.com) — same GEEP umbrella and portal-access caveats as TraderMoni
programs.notes: Same GEEP umbrella as TraderMoni/FarmerMoni — same correction (geep.nsipa.gov.ng confirmed suspended in production by a real user click-through, reverted to the live nsipa.gov.ng/geep/ info page).

programs.name: GEEP — FarmerMoni
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Farmer, typically part of an aggregator farming group/cooperative
programs.application_process: Visit the NSIPA GEEP info page, then follow the program's current application channel (no stable direct application URL found — see notes)
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (cutoffmark.ng, connectnigeria.com, haskenews.com.ng) — same GEEP umbrella and portal-access caveats as TraderMoni
programs.notes: Project Brief lists a separate general '₦300,000 FarmerMoni' figure from a secondary source (MSME Africa/Haskenews) — official NSIPA page gives the ₦50k-300k range; treat secondary figures as unconfirmed. programs.name: National Home-Grown School Feeding Programme
programs.benefit: One free meal daily per child
eligibility: Enrolled in Primary 1-3 in a public school
required_documents: none — school-administered, not individually applied for
programs.application_process: Not individually applied for — delivered through the child's public school
programs.notes: IMPORTANT for UX: this program has no individual 'apply now' link — a parent's real next step is 'confirm your child's public school participates,' not an application. Card copy/CTA needs to differ from the applied-for programs.

programs.name: National Cash Transfer Programme (NCTO)
programs.benefit: Cash transfers for welfare, nutrition, and human capital development
programs.who_its_for: Poor and vulnerable households already on the National Social Register
eligibility: Household must be enrolled in the National Social Register
programs.application_process: Not a self-service application — enrollment is via community-based targeting through NASSCO/the National Social Register, not an online form
programs.notes: CRITICAL UX ISSUE: there is no individual 'Apply now' portal link for this program — real next step is checking/registering household status on the National Social Register via community/LGA officials. AC9 ('Apply now' link on every card) needs a fallback CTA for register-based programs — e.g. 'Check your household's Social Register status' with NASSCO contact info, not a broken or misleading link.

programs.name: National Social Register (NASSCO)
programs.benefit: Not a direct benefit itself — the enrollment database that gates access to NCTO, some GVG, and other targeted cash programs
eligibility: Community-based targeting mechanism — no simple self-declared criteria found on official page
programs.application_process: Enrollment happens through community/LGA-level targeting exercises, not individual online application
programs.notes: Same CTA issue as NCTO. Consider merging NCTO + National Social Register into one card in the app to avoid presenting two near-duplicate 'apply' dead ends.

programs.name: Grant for Vulnerable Groups (GVG)
programs.benefit: Grant support to reduce poverty and enhance livelihoods
eligibility: needs_verification — official page describes intent, not criteria
programs.notes: Weakest-documented program so far. Consider calling NSIPA directly (+234 802 126 6483 / +234 806 199 5335) if it's staying in the MVP 10-12.
programs.access_pathway_note: Pattern suggests registry_gated like other NSIPA vulnerable-group grants, but official page doesn't confirm the mechanism.

programs.name: Federal Scholarship Board Award
programs.agency: Federal Scholarship Board (Federal Ministry of Education)
programs.benefit: ₦450,000 (undergraduate/NCE/HND) to ₦750,000 (PhD) renewable annual award, per category (Nigerian Scholarship Award, Education Bursary Award, Commonwealth Scholarship & Fellowship Plan)
eligibility: Nigerian Awards (undergrad): 5 SSCE credits, UTME score ≥180, admission to a Nigerian university, age below 25
BEA (undergrad): 5 SSCE distinctions, UTME score ≥200, age 18-22
Nigerian Awards (postgrad): first class or upper second class degree, admission, age below 35
CSFP: postgraduate/PhD, degree-based criteria
required_documents: needs_verification — likely SSCE result, UTME result, admission letter, degree certificate for postgrad
programs.application_process: Online, free, via the Federal Ministry of Education's scholarship portal
programs.status: benefit amounts confirmed current (50% increase applied across all levels); live application window not confirmed
programs.source_url: https://education.gov.ng/federal-scholarships-board/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026) for org structure + benefit amounts; scholarship.education.gov.ng confirmed as the real portal but is JS-rendered and didn't yield eligibility/document detail on direct fetch
programs.notes: RESOLVED: found a real primary .gov.ng source (education.gov.ng/federal-scholarships-board/) confirming the Board's structure and updated benefit amounts — the old '₦300,000/year' figure and 'no primary source found' apply_url placeholder were both wrong/stale. Eligibility criteria and required documents are still the older secondary-sourced figures (unchanged, not yet re-verified against the new portal) — recheck scholarship.education.gov.ng with a JS-capable browser, or call info@education.gov.ng / +234 8163653484 before demo.

programs.name: 3MTT (3 Million Technical Talent)
programs.agency: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy / NITDA
programs.benefit: Free tech-skills training; some tracks include laptop/router/data; Talent Registry connects to paid tech jobs from ₦150,000/month
programs.who_its_for: Nigerians wanting digital/tech skills — broadly open
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Basic ability to use a smartphone or computer
programs.application_process: Register online, complete assessments, wait for selection into a training cohort. The separate Talent Registry (job placement, ₦150k+/month) has its own registration via 3MTT + Skill Ladders, distinct from training enrollment.
programs.status: training registration open on a rolling basis (no fixed close date found); the Talent Registry job-placement track's 14 May 2026 deadline has passed
programs.source_url: https://3mtt.nitda.gov.ng/ plus aggregator corroboration (msmeafricaonline.com, jobviza.com), Sept 2026
programs.notes: RESOLVED (partially): training-track registration itself appears to be open/rolling, not tied to the passed 14 May 2026 deadline — that deadline was specifically for the Talent Registry job-placement track, which appears to have run its course. Program 2, described as three cohorts totaling 270,000 places, is referenced but its own registration dates weren't confirmed against a primary source. Recheck 3mtt.nitda.gov.ng directly before demo to confirm current cohort is genuinely accepting new registrations.

programs.name: NJFP (Nigeria Jubilee Fellows Programme)
programs.agency: Federal Government of Nigeria, funded by the EU, implemented with UNDP
programs.benefit: ₦150,000/month stipend, 12-month paid placement (public or private sector)
eligibility: Nigerian citizen
Age 30 or below
Bachelor's degree or HND
Graduated not earlier than 2022
Minimum Second Class Lower (university) or Upper Credit (HND)
Completed NYSC or holds a valid exemption certificate
Currently unemployed
Willing to work full-time during the fellowship
required_documents: a short video (max 60 seconds, max 10MB) answering 'What makes YOU the ideal NJFP Fellow?'
programs.application_process: Register at njfp.ng/apply, complete the application form, upload required documents plus the short video response, and submit
programs.status: NJFP 2.0 application cycle referenced as active per UNDP and program coverage — recheck njfp.ng/apply for exact current window before demo
programs.source_url: njfp.ng/eligibility and njfp.ng/apply confirmed to exist (Sept 2026, though the site is a JS-rendered SPA so a static fetch only returned the page title); eligibility/process detail corroborated via UNDP Nigeria (undp.org/nigeria/njfp-20-coming-heres-everything-you-need-know-get-ready-apply), a co-implementing partner, plus consistent secondary coverage
programs.notes: UPGRADED from needs_verification: eligibility criteria now corroborated by UNDP Nigeria (a program co-implementer, not just a random aggregator), and the specific apply flow — including the distinctive video-submission requirement — is consistent across sources, which is a strong signal it's accurate. Still worth a final live check of njfp.ng/apply close to demo day since the exact page content couldn't be rendered by an automated fetch (JS SPA).

programs.name: NHIA Vulnerable Group Fund (VGF)
programs.benefit: Free/subsidized health insurance — premium paid on the beneficiary's behalf by government, state agency, or NGO
programs.who_its_for: Pregnant women, children, elderly, persons with disabilities, indigent individuals who cannot pay premiums
eligibility: 'Vulnerable' + inability to pay premiums — no self-declared checklist published
programs.application_process: NOT a self-service individual application — coverage is arranged through State Social Health Insurance Agencies or a sponsoring government/NGO, not applied for directly online
programs.apply_url: https://www.nhia.gov.ng/ (general site — no individual VGF application page found)
programs.notes: SAME CTA PROBLEM as NCTO/National Social Register/GVG — no individual online application exists. Real next step is 'contact your State Social Health Insurance Agency,' not an Apply-now link. Fourth program hitting this pattern.

programs.name: SDoH Fund for Cancer Patients
programs.agency: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
programs.benefit: ₦100,000 grant per verified beneficiary (transport, accommodation, feeding) from an initial ₦50 million fund
programs.who_its_for: Cancer patients facing financial/social barriers to accessing treatment
eligibility: needs_verification — no published self-declared criteria; verification appears to run through a Technical Working Group, likely via treatment centers
programs.application_process: needs_verification — over 400 people had already applied and 200+ been verified at launch; exact application channel (online form vs. through hospital/oncology center) not found
programs.notes: FLAG: total fund (₦50M ÷ ₦100k) covers roughly 500 people nationwide, and 400+ had already applied at launch — likely oversubscribed. Presenting this as a normal 'you qualify' card risks false expectations. Consider dropping from MVP, or labeling capacity explicitly if kept.
programs.access_pathway_note: Verification appears to run through treatment centers / a Technical Working Group — likely institution-referred, not public self-service, but unconfirmed.

programs.name: HOPE-EDU / HOPE-PHC / SOLID
programs.agency: UBEC / Federal Ministry of Education & Health, financed by World Bank + Global Partnership for Education
programs.benefit: NOT an individual benefit — large-scale financing (HOPE-EDU alone is ~US$552M) transferred to STATE GOVERNMENTS conditional on the state meeting policy/budget benchmarks
programs.who_its_for: State governments and education/health systems, not individual citizens
eligibility: A state qualifies if its FY26 budget is prepared under the national Chart of Accounts with an education/health program segment, approved by the State Assembly, and published online by 31 Jan 2026 — this is a state-level policy condition, not something an individual meets
required_documents: not applicable — no individual application exists
programs.application_process: not applicable — individuals cannot apply to this program
programs.notes: CRITICAL FLAG: this is a systemic, state-to-government financing instrument, not an individual-facing benefit — structurally incompatible with ClaimAm's entire 'does this person qualify' model. There is no eligibility a citizen meets and no application a citizen submits. Recommend removing from the MVP program list entirely and replacing with a genuine individual-facing program.
programs.access_pathway_note: No individual pathway exists — state-level financing only. Should not be shown as a user-facing card at all.

programs.name: MTN Foundation Scholarship
programs.benefit: ₦300,000/year until graduation (subject to meeting grade/upskilling requirements), across three tracks: Science & Technology (STS), Scholarship for Blind Students (SBS), and Top 10 UTME
programs.who_its_for: Undergraduates in Nigerian public tertiary institutions — STEM/medical students (STS), blind students (SBS), or Nigeria's top 10 JAMB UTME scorers regardless of course
eligibility: STS: 300-level STEM students or 400-level medical students at a public institution, minimum CGPA 3.0/4.0
SBS: 200-300 level blind students at a public institution, minimum CGPA 2.5 (university) or 2.0 (polytechnic)
Top 10 UTME: automatic qualification for Nigeria's top 10 JAMB UTME scorers, any course, any institution type
required_documents: needs_verification for exact list — likely admission letter, JAMB result, current CGPA/transcript, means of ID
programs.application_process: Apply online via the official MTN Foundation scholarship form
programs.source_url: https://www.mtn.ng/scholarships/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026) — MTN's own corporate domain, confirmed open with detailed eligibility
programs.notes: Strongest of the newly-added scholarships — real corporate domain, detailed published eligibility, confirmed currently open (unlike several other programs in this dataset). 400 STS + 100 SBS + 10 Top-UTME slots annually per secondary coverage.

programs.name: PTDF Scholarship (In-Country & Overseas)
programs.benefit: In-Country: ₦700,000/year + a laptop, for bachelor's/master's/PhD at accredited Nigerian universities. Overseas: fully-funded MSc/PhD (tuition, return airfare, accommodation/living allowance, health insurance) at partner universities in the UK, Germany, France, or Malaysia
programs.who_its_for: Nigerian students in priority fields (engineering, geosciences, energy studies, environmental sciences, technology development) at bachelor's, master's, or PhD level
eligibility: needs_verification for exact criteria — likely Nigerian citizenship, admission/enrollment in an eligible priority field, academic performance threshold
required_documents: needs_verification — likely admission letter, transcripts, means of ID; overseas track likely requires an offer from a partner university
programs.application_process: Create an applicant account and apply online via the PTDF scholarship portal
programs.status: 2026 cycle applications closed 5 June 2026; reopens annually — recheck before demo
programs.source_url: https://scholarship.ptdf.gov.ng/ (fetched directly, Sept 2026 — confirmed real portal with PTDF branding, account creation/login live) plus aggregator corroboration (msmeafricaonline.com, scholarshipregion.com) for benefit amounts and deadline
programs.notes: Real federal agency (.gov.ng-pattern domain), portal confirmed operational, but exact eligibility criteria and required documents weren't retrievable via automated fetch (multi-page portal). Large benefit amount makes this worth including despite the verification gap — recheck the Guidelines page directly before demo.

programs.name: NNPC/Chevron JV National Merit Scholarship
programs.agency: NNPC Limited / Chevron Nigeria Limited (CNL) Joint Venture
programs.benefit: ₦200,000/year, renewable each academic year until graduation (subject to continued eligibility)
programs.who_its_for: Full-time 200-level undergraduates in accredited Nigerian universities, in eligible courses (Engineering, Medicine, Law, Pharmacy, Computer Science, Accountancy, Agriculture, Architecture, Mass Communication, Environmental Studies, Geology, Business Administration, and related disciplines); a separate category exists for visually impaired students
eligibility: Full-time 200-level student in an accredited Nigerian university
Minimum CGPA of 3.5/5.0 (or equivalent)
At least six O'Level credits obtained in one sitting
Studying an eligible course (see who_its_for)
required_documents: needs_verification for exact list — likely admission letter, O'Level result, current CGPA/transcript, means of ID
programs.application_process: Apply online via the Scholastica platform (the shared application system used by several NNPC joint-venture scholarships, including Chevron, Shell, and Renaissance)
programs.status: 2026 cycle applications closed 30 June 2026; reopens annually — recheck before demo
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (edugist.org, scholarsworld.ng, masteredu.com.ng) converge consistently; the Scholastica platform itself was independently corroborated as the genuine official channel by multiple unrelated sources including explicit anti-scam warnings naming this exact domain ('CNL does NOT assign representatives or agents... avoid look-alike domains')
programs.notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: an initial automated fetch of candidate.scholastica.ng read as a sparse, hard-to-verify site — a second independent search corroborated it as the real shared platform for multiple legitimate oil-JV scholarships (NNPC/Chevron, NNPC/Shell/SNEPCo, NNPC/Renaissance), including official-sounding anti-scam guidance pointing to this exact domain. Treat this corroboration as reasonably strong but not equivalent to a direct fetch of Chevron's or NNPC's own site confirming it — worth a final human check before demo, precisely because scholarship scams are common in Nigeria and this kind of shared-platform pattern is also what a convincing scam would look like.

programs.name: Shell (SPDC JV) National Merit Scholarship Award
programs.agency: Shell Petroleum Development Company (SPDC), on behalf of the NNPC/SPDC/TotalEnergies/NAOC Joint Venture
programs.who_its_for: 200-level Nigerian undergraduates (i.e. students who have just completed their first year)
eligibility: 200-level student (just completed first year)
Minimum CGPA around 2.5
National Merit Award (NM) category open to all Nigerians; Areas of Operation Merit Award (OM) category is for indigenes of Abia, Bayelsa, Delta, Imo, or Rivers States
Shortlisting is based on SSCE and JAMB/UTME results, followed by an aptitude test
required_documents: needs_verification for exact list — likely SSCE result, JAMB result, admission letter, means of ID
programs.application_process: Apply online via the Scholastica platform, then sit an aptitude test if shortlisted (over 4,000 applicants sit this test annually)
programs.status: needs_verification_now — exact 2026 cycle window not confirmed against a primary source
programs.source_url: Aggregator sources (scholarafrika.com, o3schools.com, universities.ng, edugaze.com.ng) converge consistently on eligibility and benefit; same Scholastica platform corroboration as the NNPC/Chevron entry
programs.notes: Same Scholastica-platform caveat as NNPC/Chevron — reasonably corroborated but not directly fetched from Shell's own site. Narrower eligibility than most other programs in this dataset (200-level only, one-time application window per cohort) — worth flagging to the user that this is a narrower fit than it might first appear.
